takes.action: The skater in the red cap rolls along the coping of the empty bowl, knees soft, arms loose, his navy ORVO skate shoes big in the fisheye foreground while his dachshund trots behind.

Fisheye at ground level following the board: he pushes and carves across the sun-baked concrete, both ORVO shoes shifting on the grip tape, the concrete curving and rushing beneath; his one dog, a small smooth-coated dachshund of a single solid ginger-red colour all over with a plain dark collar trots after him a few metres back. Only the two of them are in the park.

He pops a kickflip off the concrete hip, the board spins once beneath his shoes, he catches it, lands with a clack and rolls on with a quick grin. The fisheye camera follows from below; his one dog, a small smooth-coated dachshund of a single solid ginger-red colour all over with a plain dark collar comes running up behind him. Only the two of them are in the park.

He ollies onto the brutalist ledge and grinds it straight toward the lens, coming closer and growing bigger in the frame the whole time, front shoe pressing the nose, concrete dust kicking up; at the ledge's end, right in front of the low fisheye, he pops off and rolls past the camera. The park behind him is empty: only him, the concrete and the sky.

He cruises across the flat and his dachshund sprints alongside the board, little legs pumping, ears flying; he looks down at it and laughs, slowing so it can keep up. The fisheye tracks low with them.

He sits on the bowl's coping catching his breath, one ORVO shoe on the tail of the board, scratching the panting dachshund's ears as it licks his hand; he laughs and looks out over the park. The fisheye stays low and still.
